lead.headline: Alibaba ships Qwen4-Max: a 1M-context flagship at $1.50 / $4.50, with open Qwen4 weights promised
lead.summary: Out of a five-day preview, the first full Qwen4 model is a new MoE with native vision (text, image and video in) and is now on the pay-as-you-go QwenCloud API. Alibaba says it beats Qwen3.8-Max with up to about 50% fewer tokens and over 60% lower average cost per task, and shows it ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 on some tests such as DeepSWE. Artificial Analysis puts it at 43 on its Intelligence Index, below Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon but above Haiku 5.5. Smaller open-weight Qwen4 models are due later.

number_of_day.label: Signatures on the "Stand with Jensen" petition by Sunday night, up from 115,000 a day earlier. The FT reports Huang has discussed a return as Nvidia CEO with close confidants, while the board's investigation continues.

news.headline: OpenAI opens a science blog with a GPT-6 Astra-assisted lattice Standard Model proof
news.summary: The first guest post, by UC Santa Barbara physicist Nathaniel Craig, describes a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of the Standard Model. Craig says Astra turned his strategy into a construction and led the detailed proof. He calls it a beginning: open questions such as reflection positivity remain, and outside experts have not yet endorsed it. Published Sunday.

news.headline: Old Bitly links in Burger King, McDonald's and Trump tweets were re-registered and hijacked
news.summary: Short links from 2011-era tweets were registered again on Sunday and pointed at jarring pages such as Wikipedia's list of Nazi concentration camps; one quote post passed 2 million views within hours. Bitly confirmed an issue that "allowed bad actors to repurpose certain old, inactive links", suspended the accounts and is disabling the links. Of 97 Bitly links in Trump's 2009–2013 tweets, 56 were created after the tweets they sit in.

news.headline: GPT-5.6 Sol found a one-click universal XSS in uBlock Origin
news.summary: A malicious site could leak the extension's internal ID, embed uBO's element picker in an invisible iframe and trick a click into adding a trusted filter, which can run JavaScript on any site. It hit the Firefox MV2 version, with a milder variant in uBO Lite, and is now fixed. The researcher verified the bug himself and says Claude wrote most of the proof-of-concept code.

news.headline: Helsinki's Intergrid raises €23.5M for an "autopilot" that runs factory energy systems
news.summary: The round is co-led by Nordic industrial-tech fund Kvanted and state investor Tesi, with Lifeline Ventures and True Ventures joining. Autopilot runs at 100+ sites (customers include Snellman, Atria, Lindström and Vatajankoski) and sits ML predictions on top of rule-based logic, with agents for monitoring, so operators supervise rather than press buttons.

x_posts.name: Guillermo Rauch
x_posts.text:
Introducing 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝: https://t.co/YaLEMbmKwf.

A hermetic, pixel-perfect X post renderer in safe Rust / wasm. Zero browser, network, filesystem, system fonts. Renders a post to PNG in ~1ms…

It was conceived from the ground up around 'verification engineering', and the result speaks for itself.
x_posts.why: An "autorepo": a Chrome oracle checks tens of thousands of layout rules and files PRs for agents to fix.

x_posts.name: elvis
x_posts.text:
This might surprise many new to AI. The best agentic systems I have built and seen other top engineers build involve lots of boring deterministic steps.

You can't just throw more LLM agents at every problem and expect reliability to improve. Every error will compound into more errors.
x_posts.why: A good counterweight to "just add more agents": classifiers, verifiers and evals still do the heavy lifting.

x_posts.name: Ethan Mollick
x_posts.text:
I think often about the fact that almost everyone working in the West has lived in a quite stable socio-technical period

Only 1 job out of 270 in the 1950 census is now obsolete (elevator operator)

2026 is similar to 1957 in a way that 1969 was not from 1900.

That may change.
x_posts.why: A historical frame for how unusual a fast-changing job market would actually be.

writers_corner.title: Writer and podcaster Daniel Ford on balancing the home office and dad mode
writers_corner.take: With a day job, a one-person podcast network and two kids under five, Ford keeps his creative work alive by keeping it short and streamlined, and lets his old fiction ambitions wait.
writers_corner.quote: Those creative neurons are flickering, just in a different way.
